55296.subject: Chemistry
55296.text: Which from following is a correct decreasing order of water solubilities of organic compounds?
55296.sol: Decreasing order of water solubility: Alcohols > Amines > Alkanes Water solubility depends on the ability to form hydrogen bonds. Alcohols contain a polar O-H group, forming strong hydrogen bonds with water due to oxygen's high electronegativity ( O 3.44 ). Amines with N-H groups form moderately strong hydrogen bonds, though nitrogen's lower electronegativity ( N 3.04 ) results in weaker bonding than alcohols. Alkanes are nonpolar and cannot form hydrogen bonds, exhibiting only London dispersion forces.

56353.text: Which group elements have the smallest atomic radii in their respective periods?
56353.sol: In a given period, the atomic radius decreases from left to right as the effective nuclear charge increases. This trend continues up to group 17 (halogens). For group 18 (noble gases), the atomic radius is expressed as van der Waals radius since they do not form covalent bonds under normal conditions. Since van der Waals radii are always larger than covalent radii, group 18 elements have larger radii than group 17 elements. 70908.sol: Sponges belong to the phylum Porifera and exhibit a cellular level of organization. During the cell division phase, the rate of growth is relatively slow, representing the lag phase of the growth curve. During the cell elongation phase, cells undergo rapid enlargement, increased vacuolation, and new cell wall deposition. 71447.subject: Biology
71447.text: Which enzyme is responsible for phosphorylation of glucose with ATP?
71447.sol: The first step of glycolysis involves the phosphorylation of glucose to form glucose-6-phosphate. This reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme hexokinase, which uses ATP as the phosphate donor. Phosphofructokinase catalyzes the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. Aldolase catalyzes the cleavage of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate into two three-carbon sugars. Phosphohexose isomerase catalyzes the isomerization of glucose-6-phosphate to fructose-6-phosphate. Answer: Hexokinase

Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
83940.sol: The correct answer is option (2) as specific Bt toxin genes were isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis and incorporated into the several crop plants such as cotton. 84147.sol: In the alveoli, where there is high pO 2 , low pCO 2 , lesser H + concentration, and lower temperature, the factors are all favourable for the formation of oxxhaemoglobin, whereas, in the tissues, where low pO 2 , high pCO 2 , high H + concentration and higher temperature exist, the conditions are favourable for dissociation of oxygen from the oxyhaemoglobin.

Balanoglossus does not possess a notochord whereas Branchiostoma being a chordate possesses notochord that persists throughout life.

123088.subject: Botany
123088.text: An example of a seed with endosperm, perisperm and caruncle is -

123932.subject: Botany
123932.text: Post mitotic gap phase is characterised by all, except
123932.sol: Post mitotic gap phase is characterised by all except synthesis of histone proteins. Histone proteins are synthesised in S-phase. S-phase is called invisible phase of the cell cycle as replicated chromosomes are not visible at this stage.

124239.subject: Botany
124239.text: DNA Packaging Details A. Nucleosome 1. DNA wrapped around histone proteins B. Chromatin Fiber 2. Visible during cell division C. Chromosome 3. Approximately two meters long in a human cell D. DNA Thread Length 4. Highly extended form of chromatin
124239.sol: Nucleosomes are DNA wrapped around histones.Chromatin fibers are the extended form.Chromosomes are visible during cell division.DNA thread length in a human cell is about two meters.

124505.subject: Botany
124505.text: What type of curve is obtained when the length of an organ undergoing arithmetic growth is plotted against time?
124505.sol: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. The simplest expression of arithmetic growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate .On plotting the length of the organ against time, a linear curve is obtained.

124850.subject: Botany
124850.sol: Richmond and Lang 1967 observed that degradation of protein and chlorophyll was delayed in the detached leaves of Xanthium, if there was cytokinin in the medium.

124895.subject: Botany
124895.text: Root hair absorbs water from soil through
124895.sol: Root hair absorbs water from soil through osmosis. Osmosis is a special type of diffusion of a liquid, when solvent moves through a semipermeable membrane from a place of higher diffusion pressure to a place of lower diffusion pressure.

124920.subject: Botany
124920.text: What structures do plants use for gaseous exchange?
124920.sol: Yes, plants require O2 for respiration to occur and they also give out CO2. Hence, plants have systems in place that ensure the availability of O2. Plants, unlike animals, have no specialized organs for gaseous exchange but they have stomata and lenticels for this purpose. There are several reasons why plants can get along without respiratory organs. First, each plant part takes care of its own gas-exchange needs. There is very little transport of gases from one plant part to another. Second, plants do not present

125033.subject: Botany
options: A- 1,3 bisphosphoglyceric acid, B- Fructose 1, 6-bisphosphate, C- Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate
A- Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, B- 1,3 bisphosphoglyceric acid, C- 2-phosphoglycerate

125524.subject: Botany
125524.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Julius von Sachs provided evidence for production of glucose when plants grow Reason: He found that the green parts in plants is where glucose is made, and that the glucose is usually stored as starch.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125524.sol: Julius von Sachs provided evidence for production of glucose when plants grow. Glucose is usually stored as starch. His later studies showed that the green substance in plants (chlorophyll as we know it now) is located in special bodies (later called chloroplasts) within plant cells. He found that the green parts in plants is where glucose is made, and that the glucose is usually stored as starch.

125536.subject: Botany
125536.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: A proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane as well as a measurable decrease in pH in the lumen is observed Reason: The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the thylakoid side of the membrane
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125536.sol: Within the chloroplast, protons in the stroma decrease in number, while in the lumen there is accumulation of protons. This creates a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane as well as a measurable decrease in pH in the lumen.

125556.subject: Botany
125556.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Photorespiration does not synthesize sugars 2. In photorespiration occuring in C3 plants RuBP is converted to C3 plants 3. There is a parabolic relationship between incident light and CO2 fixation rates at low light intensities. 4. The light saturation occurs at 10 per cent of the full sunlight.
125556.sol: In the photorespiratory pathway, there is neither synthesis of sugars, nor of ATP. Rather it results in the release of CO2 with the utilisation of ATP.

125787.subject: Botany
125787.text: What is the main focus of the observation described in the paragraph?
options: The shape and attachment of anthers
125787.sol: the two parts of a typical stamen – the long and slender stalk called the filament, and the terminal generally bilobed structure called the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus or the petal of the flower. The number and length of stamens are variable in flowers of different species. If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. Careful observa

125868.subject: Botany
125868.text: What is a significant advantage of cleistogamous flowers mentioned in the paragraph?
options: Producing assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators
125868.sol: Autogamy: In this type, pollination is achieved within the same flower. Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower lie close to each other so that self-pollination can occur. Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers – chasmogamous flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma, and cleistogamous flowers which do not open at all. In such flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other. W

126644.subject: Botany
126644.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. A fatty acid has a carboxyl group attached to an R group 2. Palmitic acid has 14 carbons including carboxyl carbon 3. Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon 4. Lipids are generally water insoluble. 5. Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon.
126644.sol: A fatty acid has a carboxyl group attached to an R group. Palmitic acid has 16 carbons including carboxyl carbon. Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon

126732.subject: Botany
126732.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Lecithin is classified as a phospholipid and is found in cell membranes. Reason (R): The structure of lecithin contains phosphorus and a phosphorylated organic compound. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
126732.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because lecithin is a well-known example of a phospholipid that serves as a key structural component of cell membranes. Reason (R) is correct because phospholipids are defined chemically by the presence of phosphorus and a phosphorylated organic compound in their structure. Since the presence of the phosphorylated organic compound is the exact chemical basis for classifying lecithin as a phospholipid, (R) provides the correct explanation for (A). Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R)

126815.subject: Botany
126815.text: Primary proteins are also called as polypeptides because :
options: They are polymers of peptide monomers
Successive amino acids are joined by peptide bonds
126815.sol: Primary structure in proteins are continuous, in which successive amino acids are added with the help of peptide bond formation. It is simplest yet generally non-Functional structure of proteins.

127074.subject: Botany
127074.text: Drinking of mineral water with very low level of pesticides (about 0.02 ppm ) for long periods may:
options: cause leukemia (blood cancer) in most people
lead to accumulation of pesticide residues in body fat.

127627.subject: Botany
127627.text: Can a given organism occupy more than one trophic level simultaneously?
127627.sol: Any calculations of energy content, biomass or numbers, has to include all organisms at that trophic level. No generalisations we make will be true if we take only a few individuals at any trophic level into account . Also a given organism may occupy more than one trophic level simultaneously. One must remember that the trophic level represents a functional level, not a species as such. A given species may occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time; for example, a sparrow is a primary

127772.subject: Botany
127772.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Saprophytes play a vital role in ecosystems but are not given any place in ecological pyramids. Reason (R): Saprophytes are exclusively primary producers and form the base of the detritus food chain. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given bel
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
127772.sol: Assertion (A) is a correct statement. One of the major limitations of ecological pyramids is that saprophytes (decomposers) are not given any place in them, despite their vital role in the ecosystem. Reason (R) is an incorrect statement. Saprophytes are heterotrophic organisms (decomposers) that meet their energy and nutrient requirements by degrading dead organic matter or detritus. They are not primary producers. Primary producers are autotrophs. Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct. Answer: (A) is co

128823.subject: Zoology
128823.text: What is the result of erythroblastosis fetalis on the baby?
options: The baby does not get affected.
The baby could get fatal or suffer from severe anaemia and jaundice.
128823.sol: the surface of RBCs of majority (nearly 80 per cent) of humans. Such individuals are called Rh positive (Rh+ve) and those in whom this antigen is absent are called Rh negative (Rh-ve). An Rh-ve person, if exposed to Rh+ve blood, will form specific antibodies against the Rh antigens. Therefore, Rh group should also be matched before transfusions. A special case of Rh incompatibility (mismatching) has been observed between the Rh-ve blood of a pregnant mother with Rh+ve blood of the foetus. Rh antigens of the foetus

129047.subject: Zoology
129047.text: Match List I with List II. List I List II (A) Spleen (I) Enzyme that converts inactive fibrinogens into fibrins (B) Fibrin (II) Graveyard of RBCs (C) Thrombin (III) Enzyme complex required for conversion of prothrombin (D) Thrombokinase (IV) Network of threads trapping dead formed elements Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
129047.sol: Spleen is known as the graveyard of RBCs. Fibrins form a network of threads in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped. Thrombin is the enzyme that converts inactive fibrinogens present in the plasma into fibrins. Thrombokinase is the enzyme complex required to convert inactive prothrombin into active thrombin. Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III). Swapping the roles of fibrin and thrombin or thrombin and thrombokinase are common points of confusion in the coagu

129469.subject: Zoology
129469.text: What are the excretory functions performed by the antennal glands in crustaceans?
options: Both nitrogenous waste removal and osmoregulation
129469.sol: A survey of animal kingdom presents a variety of excretory structures. In most of the invertebrates, these structures are simple tubular forms whereas vertebrates have complex tubular organs called kidneys. Some of these structures are mentioned here. Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes (Flatworms, e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate – Amphioxus. Protonephridia are primarily concerned with ionic and fluid volume regulation, i.e., osmoregulation.

129506.subject: Zoology
129506.text: What is the average amount of blood filtered by the kidneys per minute?
129506.sol: The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called glomerular filtration. On an average, 1100-1200 ml of blood is filtered by the kidneys per minute which constitute roughly 1/5th of the blood pumped out by each ventricle of the heart in a minute. The glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood through 3 layers, i.e., the endothelium of glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman’s capsule and a basement membrane between these

129614.subject: Zoology
129614.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: DCT is formed from Henle's loop Reason: The ascending limb continues to form DCT
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
129614.sol: A hairpin shaped Henle’s loop is the next part of the tubule which has a descending and an ascending limb. The ascending limb continues as another highly coiled tubular region called distal convoluted tubule (DCT).

129621.subject: Zoology
129621.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Glomerulus is formed by efferent arteriole 2. Bowman's capsule encloses glomerulus 3. Glomerulus alongwith Bowman’s capsule, is called the malpighian body or renal corpuscle 4. The tubule continues further to form a highly coiled network – proximal convoluted tubule
129621.sol: The renal tubule begins with a double walled cup-like structure called Bowman’s capsule, which encloses the glomerulus. Glomerulus alongwith Bowman’s capsule, is called the malpighian body or renal corpuscle. The tubule continues further to form a highly coiled network – proximal convoluted tubule

129768.subject: Zoology
129768.sol: Urine formation takes place in kidney. It includes glomerular filtration (ultrafiltration), selective reabsorption and tubular secretion. Urine is stored temporarily in urinary bladder.

130100.subject: Zoology
130100.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Under normal physiological conditions, every 100 ml of oxygenated blood delivers around 20 ml of O ₂ to the tissues. Reason (R): In the tissues, low pO ₂ , high pCO ₂ , high H ^+ concentration and higher temperature exist, which are favourable for dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin. In the
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
130100.sol: Assertion (A) is false because under normal physiological conditions, every 100 ml of oxygenated blood can deliver around 5 ml of O ₂ to the tissues, not 20 ml . While 100 ml of oxygenated blood carries about 20 ml of O ₂ , it only unloads approximately 25 % (i.e., 5 ml ) to the tissues under resting conditions. Reason (R) is true. In the tissues, conditions such as low pO ₂ , high pCO ₂ , high H ^+ concentration, and higher temperature shift the oxygen dissociation curve to the right. These factors are favourable

130415.subject: Zoology
130415.text: There are 11 pairs of ribs in a man
130415.sol: There are 12 pairs of ribs in a man.

130555.subject: Zoology
130555.text: Why did the government need to take serious measures regarding population growth?
options: To address the increase in global population
To manage the shortage of skilled professionals
To prevent an absolute scarcity of essential resources
130555.sol: Our population which was approximately 350 million at the time of our independence reached close to the billion mark by 2000 and crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011. A rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR) as well as an increase in number of people in reproducible age are probable reasons for this. Through our Reproductive Child Health (RCH) programme, though we could bring down the population growth rate, it was only marginal. According to the 2011 census report, th

131484.subject: Zoology
131484.text: What was the first organism in which semiconservative DNA replication was proven?
131484.sol: It is now proved that DNA replicates semiconservatively. It was shown first in Escherichia coli and subsequently in higher organisms, such as plants and human cells. Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl performed the following experiment in 1958: (i) They grew E. coli in a medium containing 15NH4Cl (15N is the heavy isotope of nitrogen) as the only nitrogen source for many generations. The result was that 15N was incorporated into newly synthesized DNA (as well as other nitrogen containing compounds). This heavy DNA

131875.subject: Zoology
131875.text: A researcher isolates an E. coli strain with a normal i gene, promoter, and operator, but with a nonsense mutation in the y gene that renders its product completely non-functional. If this strain is transferred from a lactose-free medium to a lactose-rich medium, what will be the primary outcome regarding the lac operon?
options: The operon will be fully induced because lactose is present in the surrounding medium.
The repressor will bind to lactose outside the cell, allowing transcription to proceed.
The z gene will be transcribed and translated normally, but permease will not be formed.
The operon will fail to be induced because lactose cannot efficiently enter the cell.
131875.sol: The lac operon consists of three structural genes: z , y , and a . The y gene codes for permease, which increases the permeability of the cell to -galactosides (lactose). For the operon to be induced, lactose must first enter the cell to bind and inactivate the repressor protein. This entry requires a functional permease enzyme. Since the mutant strain has a non-functional y gene, it cannot produce functional permease. Consequently, lactose from the medium cannot efficiently enter the cell to act as an inducer. The

132133.subject: Zoology
132133.text: What does the unmodified allele represent?
132133.sol: In the first case, the modified allele is equivalent to the unmodified allele, i.e., it will produce the same phenotype/trait, i.e., result in the transformation of substrate S. Such equivalent allele pairs are very common. But, if the allele produces a non-functional enzyme or no enzyme, the phenotype may be effected. The phenotype/trait will only be dependent on the functioning of the unmodified allele. The unmodified (functioning) allele, which represents the original phenotype is the dominant allele and the mod

132329.subject: Zoology
132329.text: Select the correct statement for the given pedigree.

132397.subject: Zoology
132397.text: Trait/Disorder Type of Inheritance A. ABO blood group 1. Multiple alleles B. Human skin color 2. Polygenic inheritance C. Sickle-cell anemia 3. Pleiotropy D. Height in humans 4. Codominance
132397.sol: ABO blood group: Multiple alleles (IA, IB, and i alleles). Human skin color: Polygenic inheritance (influenced by multiple genes). Sickle-cell anemia: Pleiotropy (a single gene affects multiple traits, such as anemia, pain, and organ damage). Height in humans: Polygenic inheritance (influenced by multiple genes leading to continuous variation in height).

132846.subject: Zoology
132846.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. The first human-like being was called Homo habilis. 2. The brain capacities of Homo habilis were between 650-800cc. 3. Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed the next stage, i.e., Homo erectus about 1.5 mya. 4. Homo erectus had a large brain around 900cc.
132846.sol: Homo erectus probably ate meat. The Neanderthal man with a brain size of 1400cc lived in near east and central Asia between 1,00,000-40,000 years back. They used hides to protect their body and buried their dead. Homo sapiens arose in Africa and moved across continents and developed into distinct races. During ice age between 75,000-10,000 years ago modern Homo sapiens arose. Pre-historic cave art developed about 18,000 years ago. One such cave paintings by Pre-historic humans can be seen at Bhimbetka rock shelter

133165.subject: Zoology
133165.text: What are the other bacterial diseases in humans besides pneumonia?
133165.sol: Many viruses also cause diseases in human beings. Rhino viruses represent one such group of viruses which cause one of the most infectious human ailments – the common cold. Dysentery, Plague, Diphtheria, etc. are some of the other bacterial diseases in humans besides pneumoniA) . Malaria is caused by a tiny protozoan named Plasmodium. Malignant malaria, which is the most serious form of malaria, is caused by Plasmodium falciparum. Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of

133419.subject: Zoology
133419.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Plasmodium falciparum is responsible for malignant malaria, the most serious form of malaria. 2. Plasmodium enters the human body as merozoites through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. 3. The rupture of white blood cells (WBCs) during malaria releases haemozoin, causing chills and high fever. 4. The malarial parasite completes its life
133419.sol: Plasmodium falciparum is responsible for malignant malaria, the most serious form of malaria. Plasmodium enters the human body as merozoites through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. The rupture of red blood cells (RBCs) during malaria releases haemozoin, causing chills and high fever. The malarial parasite completes its life cycle in only one host: the human. The female Anopheles mosquito acts as both the vector and a host for the malarial parasite.

133534.subject: Zoology
133534.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Heroin acts as a depressant and slows down body functions. Reason (R): Heroin is chemically diacetylmorphine, which is obtained by the methylation of morphine. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
133534.sol: Assertion (A) is true because heroin (commonly called smack) is a depressant and slows down body functions. Reason (R) is false because heroin is chemically diacetylmorphine, which is obtained by the acetylation of morphine, not by its methylation. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false. Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

133873.subject: Zoology
133873.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Lactobacillus is a fungi Reason: Lactobacillus coverts buttermilk into curd
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
133873.sol: Microorganisms such as Lactobacillus and others commonly called lactic acid bacteria (LAB) grow in milk and convert it to curd.

134087.subject: Zoology
134087.text: What type of insects are affected by the Bt toxin produced by Bacillus thuringiensis?
134087.sol: Bt Cotton: Some strains of Bacillus thuringiensis produce proteins that kill certain insects such as lepidopterans (tobacco budworm, armyworm), coleopterans (beetles) and dipterans (flies, mosquitoes). B. thuringiensis forms protein crystals during a particular phase of their growth. These crystals contain a toxic insecticidal protein. Why does this toxin not kill the Bacillus? Actually, the Bt toxin protein exist as inactive protoxins but once an insect ingest the inactive toxin, it is converted into an active for

134221.subject: Zoology
134221.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The White Revolution succeeded in tripling the food supply and it was enough to feed the growing human population. 2. Increased yields have partly been due to the use of improved crop varieties, but mainly due to the use of better management practices and use of agrochemicals. 3. However, for farmers in the developing world, agrochemicals are often too e
134221.sol: The Green Revolution succeeded in tripling the food supply and it was not enough to feed the growing human population. Increased yields have partly been due to the use of improved crop varieties, but mainly due to the use of better management practices and use of agrochemicals. However, for farmers in the developing world, agrochemicals are often too expensive, and further increase in yield with existing varieties are not possible using conventional breeding.

134230.subject: Zoology
134230.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. A nematode Meloidegyne incognitia infects the stems of tobacco plants and causes a great reduction in yeild. 2. A novel strategy was adopted to prevent this infestation which was based on the process of RNA interference. 3. This method involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of th
134230.sol: A nematode Meloidegyne incognitia infects the roots of tobacco plants and causes a great reduction in yeild. A novel strategy was adopted to prevent this infestation which was based on the process of RNA interference. RNAi takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defense. This method involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA (silencing). The source of this complementary RNA could be from an infection by virus

134317.subject: Zoology
134317.text: A molecular biologist uses a standard radioactive probe, which is complementary to a normal (wild-type) gene, to screen a patient's cell clone for a suspected cancer-causing mutation. After allowing the probe to hybridize with the cellular DNA, autoradiography is performed. The resulting photographic film shows clear and distinct radioactive spots corresponding to the clone. What does this observation indicate about
options: The cells contain the normal, unmutated gene, as the probe successfully hybridized with it.
The cells contain the mutated cancer-causing gene, which actively bound to the radioactive probe.
The probe failed to undergo hybridization, causing the unbound radioactive material to expose the film.
The cells lack the target gene entirely, allowing the probe to precipitate and form spots.
134317.sol: In molecular diagnosis using autoradiography, a standard radioactive probe is designed to be complementary to the normal (wild-type) gene. If the photographic film shows clear radioactive spots, it indicates that the radioactive probe has successfully hybridized with the DNA in the cell clone. This successful hybridization proves that the cells possess the normal, unmutated gene sequence that is complementary to the probe. If the gene were mutated, it would lack complementarity with the standard probe, hybridizatio

134610.subject: Zoology
134610.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Foreign DNA and vector DNA cut with the help of ligase. Reason: Ligase act on sugar phosphate backbone of DNA.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
134610.sol: The cutting of DNA at specific locations became possible with the discovery of the so-called molecular scissors’– restriction enzymes. The cut piece of DNA was then linked with the plasmid DNA. These plasmid DNA act as vectors to transfer the piece of DNA attached to it. The linking of antibiotic resistance gene with the plasmid vector became possible with the enzyme DNA ligase, which acts on cut DNA molecules and joins their ends.

134621.subject: Zoology
134621.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. When the transformed cells on agar plates containing ampicillin are spread, both transformed and non transformed cells will grow 2. Restriction enzymes are used in isolation and separation of DNA from other macromolecules 3. Downstream processing is one of the steps of rDNA technology 4.Disarmed pathogen vectors are also used in transfer of rDNA into the
134621.sol: Since the DNA is enclosed within the membranes, we have to break the cell open to release DNA along with other macromolecules such as RNA, proteins, polysaccharides and also lipids. This can be achieved by treating the bacterial cells/plant or animal tissue with enzymes such as lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cells), chitinase (fungus).

134898.subject: Zoology
134898.text: Read the following statements regarding the methods of introducing recombinant DNA into host cells: (A) In micro-injection, recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell. (B) Biolistics or gene gun method uses high-velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA and is suitable for plant cells. (C) Bacterial cells are made competent to take up DNA by treating them with a specifi
134898.sol: Statements (A), (B), and (D) are correct descriptions of gene transfer methods as per NCERT. Statement (C) is incorrect because bacterial cells are made competent by treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation, such as calcium, which increases the efficiency with which DNA enters the bacterium through pores in its cell wall. Monovalent cations like sodium are not used for this purpose. Therefore, exactly three statements are correct. Answer: Three

134937.subject: Zoology
134937.text: The enzyme (a) is needed for isolating genetic material from plant cells and enzyme (b) for isolating genetic material from fungus. Choose the correct pair of options from the following:
134937.sol: Cellulase can degrade cellulosic cell wall of plant cell while chitinase is used for degrading Chitin (Fungal cellulase) for obtaining DNA from cell.

135030.subject: Zoology
135030.text: Given below is a sample of portion of DNA strand given the base sequence on the opposite strand. What is so special show in it? aligned & 5'- GAATTC...3' & 3'- CTTAAG ... 5' aligned
135030.sol: Palindromic DNA is base sequence of DNA which reads the same forward and backward. It has similar sequence in both the strands. Different types of palindromic sequences are recognised by restriction endonucleases.

6a0e277a165ae1327797b3f4.subject: Biology
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3f4.text: In the anatomy of a frog's heart, the single ventricle opens into a specialized sac-like structure located on the ventral side. Identify this structure from the given options.
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3f4.sol: The heart of a frog consists of three chambers: two atria and one ventricle. The ventricle opens into a sac-like structure on the ventral side of the heart known as the conus arteriosus. The sinus venosus is a triangular structure on the dorsal side of the heart that receives blood from the major veins (vena cava) and opens into the right atrium. Answer: Conus arteriosus

95193.subject: Botany
95193.text: In dicot stem, the xylem is
95193.sol: There are four types of primary xylem development: exarch, endarch, centrarch, and mesarch. In endarch development, the protoxylem begins its development from the innermost procambial cells located adjacent to the pith and development progresses outward. Therefore, the protoxylem is found toward the inside and metaxylem toward the outside of the stem. Endarch development is considered the most highly advanced type of primary xylem development.

95388.subject: Botany
95388.text: Metagenesis or alteration of generation can be observed in members of phylum
95388.sol: Metagenesis (or alternation of generation) Coelenterates exhibit two body forms: polyp and medusa. A. Polyp = Sessile and cylindrical like Hydra, Adamsia. B. Medusa = Free swimming, umbrella shaped like Aurelia (jelly fish). Those cnidarians in which both polyp and medusa alternates with each other, are said to exhibit metagenesis. During metagenesis, polyp (asexual stage) reproduce asexually to form medusa, whereas the medusa (sexual stage) sexually reproduce to form polyp, e.g., Obelia .

96054.subject: Botany
96054.text: Glycolipids in the plasma membrane are located at
options: Inner leaflet of the plasma membrane
The outer leaflet of the plasma membrane
Evenly distributed in the inner and outer leaflets
It varies according to cell types
96054.sol: In eukaryotes, the cell membrane is explained as a fluid mosaic model by Schleiden and Schwann. According to this model the plasma membrane is made up of lipids and proteins. The lipids are arranged in a bilayer. The lipids present are phospholipids. These are arranged in such a way that the polar heads are towards the outer side and hydrophobic ends are towards the inner side. The ratio of proteins and lipids are different in different cell types. In humans it is seen that around 40 percent is lipid and 52 percent

96078.subject: Botany
96078.text: Find the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Integral proteins are present on the surface of the membrane.
Phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer, which is the major constituent of the cell membrane.
The cell membrane of RBCs consists of 40% lipids and 52% proteins.
96078.sol: The cell membrane consists of two types of proteins: integral proteins are intrinsic proteins which are present deeply embedded in the lipid bilayer and cannot be easily removed, external proteins are present on the surface and loosely associated with the lipid bilayer.

96168.subject: Botany
96168.text: Two features present in meiosis but absent in mitosis are
options: Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between them
96168.sol: Homologous chromosomes are made up of chromosome pairs of approximately the same length, centromere position, and staining pattern, for genes with the same corresponding loci. One homologous chromosome is inherited from the organism's mother; the other is inherited from the organism's father. They have a tendency to pair with each other during meiosis and undergoes crossing over to produce new genetic recombinations.

96212.subject: Botany
96212.text: Which of these stages of mitosis is the shortest?
96212.sol: The stages of nuclear division in mitosis are prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. Prophase is the longest phase of mitosis while anaphase is the shortest phase. Anaphase is characterized by splitting of centromere and pulling of chromosomes towards the poles.

96425.subject: Botany
96425.text: Which kind of pyramid will be obtained if a small standing crop of lower trophic levels supports large standing crop of higher trophic levels?
96425.sol: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. When the lower levels have lower standing crop than the higher level, the pyramid will be inverted, as in the case of the pyramid of biomass in an aquatic ecosystem.

96712.subject: Botany
96712.text: Zinc is required for synthesis of
96712.sol: Plants obtain zinc as Zn 2+ ions. It activates various enzymes, especially carboxylases. It is also needed in the synthesis of auxin.

96809.subject: Botany
96809.text: Pentamerous actinomorphic flowers, bicarpellary ovary with oblique septa, and fruit capsule or berry are characteristic features of family
96809.sol: A pentamerous actinomorphic flower is one where the floral parts are in multiples of five and the flower can be divided into two equal halves in more than one plane. The gynoecium is bicarpellary, syncarpous, forming a superior bilocular ovary. Each locule has many ovules on axile placentation. Members of Solanaceae are characterized by the presence of an obliquely placed septum in the ovary and highly swollen placentae. The oblique septum is probably due to shifting in the position of the ovary.

96889.subject: Botany
96889.text: Which of the following characters are common in plants like Indigofera, Sesbania, groundnut, and gram?
96889.sol: Indigofera (dye), Sesbania (fodder), groundnut (oil yielding plant), and gram (pulse) all are members of the Fabaceae family which shows zygomorphic flowers due to vexillary aestivation.

96941.subject: Botany
96941.text: Among flowers of Calotropis, Tulip, Sesbania, Asparagus, Colchicine, Sweet pea, Petunia, Indigofera, Mustard, Soybean, Tobacco and groundnut how many plants have corolla with valvate aestivation?
96941.sol: Valvate aestivation is present in the members of Brassicaceae, Solanaceae and liliaceae family. Thus Calotropis, Tulip, Asparagus, Colchicine, Petunia, Mustard and Tobacco have valvate aestivation in corolla, but in liliaceae tepals have valvate aestivation.

97070.subject: Botany
97070.text: How many plants in the list given below have marginal placentation? Mustard, Gram, Tulip, Asparagus, Arhar, Sun hemp, Chilli, Colchicum, Onion, Moong, Pea, Tobacco, Lupin
97070.sol: Placentation is the arrangement of the ovules in the ovary and their attachment to it. Placentation are of various type in the angiosperms - marginal, axile, central, parietal, basal, and free central. In marginal placentation, ovules are attached to the ridge formed on the ventral suture of the ovary. It occurs in the monocarpellary and unilocular ovary. Gram, Arhar, Sun Hemp, Moong, Lupin and Pea the marginal placentation. Mustard has parietal placentation. Axile placentation is shown by Tulip, Asparagus, Colchic

97183.subject: Botany
97183.text: Arithmetic growth curve is represented by which of the following equation?
options: w t = w 0 e r t
97183.sol: In arithmetic growth, one of the daughter cells continues to divide, whereas the other differentiates into maturity following mitotic cell division. The rate of growth is constant and increase in growth occurs in arithmetic progression, i.e., 1,2,3,4,5 and so on. It can also be represented by N t = N 0 + r t.

97231.subject: Botany
97231.text: The hormone that can replace the process of vernalisation is
97231.sol: Vernalisation refers especially to the promotion of flowering by a period of low temperature. It prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and enables the plant to have sufficient time to reach maturity. Gibberellins initiate growth in plants by stimulating cell elongation, and thereby, antagonistically, it regulates the process of vernalisation.

97278.subject: Botany
97278.text: Spraying of juvenile conifers with which hormone hastens the maturity period and thus leading to early seed production?
options: The hormone which also causes bolting in some plants
The hormone which is activated during deficiency of water
The hormone which is responsible for apical dominance
The hormone which prevents apical dominance is plants
97278.sol: The hormone which also causes bolting in some plants is Gibberellin. Gibberellins are growth promoters. They were first discovered in a fungus Gibberella fujikuroi . There are many gibberellins and they are denoted as GA1, GA2, GA3 and so on. However, GA3 was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. 306802.subject: Physics
options: holes and conduction electrons continuously recombine throughout the material
holes and conduction electrons continuously recombine throughout the material except in the depletion region
new holes and conduction electrons are generated continuously throughout the material except in the depletion
new holes and conduction electrons are generated continuously throughout the material
306802.sol: In a p - n junction, thermal energy continuously generates electron-hole pairs throughout the entire material, including the depletion region. Simultaneously, the conduction electrons and holes continuously recombine throughout the entire material to maintain thermal equilibrium. Thus, both generation and recombination of charge carriers occur continuously everywhere in the p - n junction.

6a7a1ff8bac430bbf86fe6de.sol: Given, increase in internal energy, U = 6000 J Since 75 % of the total heat supplied ( Q ) is used to increase the internal energy: U = 0.75 Q Q = 6000 0.75 = 8000 J According to the first law of thermodynamics: Q = U + W W = 8000 - 6000 = 2000 J Work done in an isobaric process is given by W = P V 2000 = (2 10^5) V V = 2000 2 10^5 = 0.01 m ^3 Converting to liters: V = 0.01 1000 L = 10 L Answer: 10 L

6a7a1ff88f4dc24dc2a3f102.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff88f4dc24dc2a3f102.text: Equal moles of Helium gas and Oxygen gas are kept in separate closed containers at the same temperature. Which of the following statements correctly compares their average translational kinetic energies per molecule and their average total kinetic energies per molecule?
options: Their average translational kinetic energies are equal, but the average total kinetic energy of Oxygen is grea
Both their average translational kinetic energies and their average total kinetic energies are equal.
Their average total kinetic energies are equal, but the average translational kinetic energy of Helium is grea
Both the average translational kinetic energy and the average total kinetic energy of Oxygen are greater than
6a7a1ff88f4dc24dc2a3f102.sol: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the average translational kinetic energy per molecule for any gas is 3 2 k_B T , which depends only on the absolute temperature. Thus, since both gases are at the same temperature, their average translational kinetic energies are equal. However, the total kinetic energy per molecule depends on the degrees of freedom f , and is given by f 2 k_B T . Helium is a monatomic gas with f = 3 , so its average total kinetic energy per molecule is 3 2 k_B T . Oxygen is a diatomic gas

6a7a1ff8c899e97d46df549d.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8c899e97d46df549d.text: An electromagnetic wave is propagating along the positive x-axis. At a given instant and position, the electric field vector points along the negative y-axis. The direction of the magnetic field vector at that instant is:
6a7a1ff8c899e97d46df549d.sol: The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the vector c = E B . Given that the wave propagates along the positive x-axis, c = i . The electric field is along the negative y-axis, so E = - j . We know that c , E , and B form a mutually perpendicular right-handed triad. Therefore, the direction of the magnetic field can be found using B = c E . Substituting the given unit vectors: B = i (- j ) = -( i j ) = - k Thus, the magnetic field is along the negative z-axis. Answer: negative z-axis

6a7a1ff80dbdd82c4383ac35.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff80dbdd82c4383ac35.text: A heavy nucleus X of mass number 240 undergoes alpha decay to form a daughter nucleus Y of mass number 236 . The binding energy per nucleon for nucleus X is 7.60 MeV , for nucleus Y is 7.70 MeV , and for the alpha particle is 7.10 MeV . The total energy released in this decay process is:
6a7a1ff80dbdd82c4383ac35.sol: The energy released ( Q -value) in a nuclear reaction is equal to the difference between the total binding energy of the products and the total binding energy of the reactants. Total binding energy of parent nucleus X = 240 7.60 = 1824.0 MeV Total binding energy of daughter nucleus Y = 236 7.70 = 1817.2 MeV Total binding energy of alpha particle = 4 7.10 = 28.4 MeV Total binding energy of products = 1817.2 + 28.4 = 1845.6 MeV Q = 1845.6 - 1824.0 = 21.6 MeV Answer: 21.6 MeV

6a7a1ff87e9e64d54c5b149b.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff87e9e64d54c5b149b.text: Which of the following diketones has all its carbon atoms sp^2 hybridized and forms a continuous conjugated system?
6a7a1ff87e9e64d54c5b149b.sol: To determine the correct molecule, we must check both for conjugation and the hybridization of every carbon atom. Hex-3-ene-2,5-dione: CH₃-C(=O)-CH=CH-C(=O)-CH₃ . While the central core is conjugated, the two terminal methyl ( CH₃ ) groups contain sp^3 hybridized carbon atoms. Cyclohex-2-ene-1,4-dione: Contains a conjugated system involving one C=C bond and two C=O bonds, but the ring also contains two sp^3 hybridized CH₂ groups at positions 5 and 6. Cyclopent-4-ene-1,3-dione: Contains a C=C bond and two C=O bonds.
